posts.body:
Well... this is new.

After plenty of planning, writing, rewriting, changing my mind, and probably making my friend regret agreeing to help me with this in the first place, writtenbyskyk.com is officially live!

This website has been something I've wanted to put together for quite a while, a place where all of my stories can live under one roof, whether they're finished, currently being written, or still waiting impatiently in the back of my head.

There's still plenty I want to add as those stories grow, but for now, I'm incredibly happy to finally have a little corner of the internet to call my own.

And since you're reading this, I suppose the Updates section works too.

Welcome to my worlds!
posts.title: Apparently I have a website now.
Back to Sekari
posts.body:
Hello again! Hope you're all doing well!

It's been a little while since I launched this website, and apparently it hasn't broken yet, so I'm calling that a success.

Now that everything is up and running, I figured it's probably time I actually use this little Updates section for what it was made for: talking about what I'm writing.

And right now, that means going back to Sekari.

"The Last Druid" may be finished, but I'm definitely not finished with its world. Most of my writing time lately has been going into the second book, "The Last Druid: Rising Tide." It picks up immediately after the first book ends, so there wasn't exactly much time for anyone to recover.
I'm sure they'll be fine.
Probably.

Writing a sequel has been a surprisingly different experience from writing the first book. With "The Last Druid," I was still figuring out the world, the characters and, occasionally, what on earth I was actually doing. Now I get to return to all of it already knowing these people, which is both wonderful and mildly inconvenient when they refuse to cooperate with whatever I originally planned for them.

"Rising Tide" lets me explore parts of Sekari that the first book only touched on, bring back people from Zane's past, and spend more time with the five characters at the heart of the story now that they've somehow gone from complete strangers to something resembling a family.
A dysfunctional one, obviously.

There are also some new faces, new places and quite a few things I have been waiting a very long time to write. 
Some of those things are lovely. Some of them are not.
I'm not going to say which.

There's still plenty of "Rising Tide" left to write, and I'm deliberately not putting a deadline on it. For now, I'm enjoying being back with these characters and watching the pile of notes, half-written scenes and questionable decisions slowly turn into an actual book.

~ Sky
